body:
Full-codebase review, cross-client finding. Verified by reading both implementations.

Price input parsing diverges. Android strips every currency symbol anywhere in the string (a character loop over `€$£¥`); the web strips only one leading and one trailing symbol. So "1€5" is saved as 15.00 on Android and rejected on the web, and "€1.50€" or "€€1.50" likewise. The web file's comment asserts the opposite — "A symbol is only stripped from the ends, matching Android's parsePriceAmount, so an embedded symbol ("1€5") is left in place and correctly rejected" — so the comment is wrong, not just the code.

Fix direction: pick one grammar (stripping only the ends is the safer one), fix the comment, and add a `price-parse` group to shared-test-cases so it cannot drift again.
title: Cross-client: price input parsing diverges, and the web comment claims it does not
